title: Total L1-sacrum flexion-extension ROM under follower preload, % of 0 N value

quantity.name: ROM normalised
quantity.definition: total sagittal ROM (8 Nm flex / 6 Nm ext) as % of the same specimen's 0 N preload ROM; mean (SD)

source.authors: Patwardhan AG, Havey RM, Carandang G, Simonds J, Voronov LI, Ghanayem AJ, Meade KP, Gavin TM, Paxinos O
source.n: 21 cadaveric L1-sacrum spines (neutral path); 15 of them also with flexed path
source.sample: human cadaver ligamentous lumbar spines L1-sacrum, mild-moderate degeneration, no bridging osteophytes

protocol.summary: L1 and sacrum potted; neutral posture = top cup ~15 deg extension at 0 N/0 Nm. Flexion-extension moments applied by water flowing into bags on loading arms on the top cup, continuous cycling between 8 Nm flexion and 6 Nm extension (rate 2.8-3.1 Nm/min flexion, 2.2-2.5 Nm/min extension), >= 2 full cycles recorded (analysed cycle not stated). Follower preload 0/200/400/800/1200 N via bilateral cables through guides on L2-sacrum to a hanger; path optimised either for the neutral posture (min lordosis change, 21 specimens) or for a forward-flexed posture at 2/3 of baseline flexion ROM (15 specimens). 5 min between preload increments; load cell under sacrum; Optotrak motion of each vertebra relative to sacrum.
how_to_simulate: Model L1-sacrum; fix the sacrum; L1 free with moments applied at the top (L1) cup; start from the specimen's neutral posture

Apply a follower preload (0, 200, 400, 800, 1200 N) whose line of action passes through each segment's flexion-extension ICR / tangent to the lordotic curve (neutral-posture path); optionally the flexed-posture path
Apply flexion to 8 Nm and extension to 6 Nm under each preload
Report total sagittal ROM of L1 relative to the sacrum (full flexion to full extension) and the bilinear flexibility coefficients a1 (low flexion moments), a3 (low extension moments), a1/a2, a3/a4
protocol.notes: ROM = total L1-sacrum rotation from 8 Nm flexion to 6 Nm extension (not per level). Order of preloads not randomised; 0 N ROM repeated at end in 14 specimens was 8% larger than at start. Per-level ROM not reported.
